title: Living sustainably
examples: What is the difference between a carbon footprint and an ecological footprint?
Can I really make a difference with my daily choices?
What are the best ways to reduce energy use at home?

explain.say: Today we will learn about living sustainably for our planet.

items: It balances people, planet, and profit.

explain.say: First we look at our carbon footprint, which measures our impact.
Next we consider food choices, as what we eat matters a lot.
Travel choices also affect our planet in significant ways.
Finally, we must think about our energy choices at home.
In real life, choosing to cycle to school instead of driving is a great step.

faq.q: How big is my personal carbon footprint?
faq.a: It is the total amount of greenhouse gases caused by my actions. You can estimate it by looking at your energy use and diet.
asks: What makes up my carbon footprint?
How do I calculate my carbon footprint?

faq.q: Is eating vegetarian always the best choice?
faq.a: It is a very good choice, but local and seasonal eating is also very helpful. Reducing waste is also key.
asks: What food choices help the planet most?

faq.q: Are all forms of travel bad for the environment?
faq.a: No, public transport and walking are much better than flying or driving alone. Efficiency matters for every trip.
asks: What is the greenest way to travel?
How much does travel affect the climate?

faq.q: Does using solar power really help the environment?
faq.a: Yes, solar power generates electricity without burning fossil fuels. It is a key part of clean energy.
asks: Are solar panels good for the planet?

faq.q: If I recycle everything, is my footprint small enough?
faq.a: Recycling is important, but changing consumption habits is more powerful. Reducing what you buy is the best step.
asks: Is recycling enough to help the planet?
What is the best way to reduce waste?

facts: Fossil fuels release greenhouse gases when burned.
Local food generally has a smaller transport footprint.
Renewable energy sources include wind and solar power.
Reducing consumption is often more effective than just recycling.

quiz.say: Which activity contributes the most to a high carbon footprint?
quiz.why: Air travel burns large amounts of fuel, releasing many greenhouse gases into the atmosphere.

wrong.0: This uses human power and generates almost no emissions.
wrong.1: While good, this only addresses one small part of the overall footprint.
wrong.2: Buses are better than cars, but they still use fossil fuels.

quiz.say: To lower your food footprint, you should focus on:

options.show: Eating only meat from local farms
options.say: Eating only meat from local farms

options.show: Eating food that is out of season
options.say: Eating food that is out of season

quiz.why: Plant-based foods and items grown nearby require fewer resources and energy to produce.

wrong.0: Even local meat production can have a high methane output.
wrong.1: Long-distance transport significantly increases the carbon cost.
wrong.2: Out-of-season food often requires energy-intensive growing methods.

quiz.say: If you must travel long distances, which option is best?
quiz.why: These forms of public transport are generally more energy-efficient per person than flying.

wrong.1: This puts all the emissions onto just one vehicle.
wrong.2: Even short flights have a disproportionately large carbon output.
wrong.3: Larger vehicles use more fuel regardless of the trip length.
